content: It is essential to adhere to the prescribed schedule for this medication and attend all medical and laboratory appointments as directed. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist immediately to establish a new dosing schedule. Store the medication at room temperature, away from light and heat, ensuring it is kept below 104°F (40°C). Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into drains unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of the product when it is expired or no longer needed. This medication is typically administered by a healthcare professional through an injection into a vein. It is usually given 2 to 3 times daily for the first 2 to 3 weeks of treatment, followed by once-daily administration. The infusion is generally delivered slowly over 1 to 2 hours using an infusion pump. Do not mix this medication with other drugs. Before use, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration. To prevent kidney damage, it is crucial to stay well-hydrated while using this medication. Antiviral medications are most effective when their levels in the body remain consistent, so it is vital to follow your doctor’s instructions precisely. Do not use more of this medication or infuse it more frequently or faster than prescribed. If the medication comes into contact with your skin, rinse thoroughly with water. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, headache, diarrhea, dizziness, or swelling/pain at the injection site. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. The drug may cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk, but due to potential risks to the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose with severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. This medication is usually first administered in a hospital setting, where your condition can be closely monitored. Regular laboratory and medical tests, such as kidney function, electrolyte levels, complete blood count, and eye exams, should be conducted while using this medication. The information provided here is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
